proposals.spec_text: Diagnostics MUST route through an optional ILogger receptacle; a missing logger MUST NOT turn any operation into an error.
proposals.actual: Primary diagnostics (initialize/shutdown) route through ILogger via log_debug and correctly tolerate a missing logger (the 'missing logger is not an error' half of FR-014 is satisfied). BUT the device async-event instrumentation in drain_async_events prints via eprintln! (src/rdma.rs:459-464), bypassing the ILogger receptacle.
proposals.rationale: Classification per PHASE_B_POLICY: read the location code to judge direction. FR-014 is a correct, agreed requirement (route diagnostics through the ILogger receptacle, mirroring the initiator) and the receptacle is wired and used on the primary path. The eprintln! async-event path is a genuine (Low-severity) behavioral deviation from that correct spec, NOT a case of the spec being stale/behind the code. Correct spec + non-compliant code => ALIGN task, not BACKFILL. Do NOT weaken FR-014 to bless eprintln!. This deviation is already flagged in the spec's Known Limitations and matches the standing FR-014 align-task; re-affirmed for this run.
proposals.resolution: Add/refresh an ALIGN task (route drain_async_events diagnostics through the accept-loop ILogger handle instead of eprintln!). No source edit in this Phase-B pass (Markdown-only; .rs is out of scope).

proposals.requirement: Unspecced: device async-event instrumentation (TAG_ASYNC epoll fd, drain_async_events, async_event_name, FFI responder_async_fd/responder_drain_async_event)
proposals.actual: Under the rdma feature the accept loop multiplexes the verbs device async-event fd (TAG_ASYNC in the epoll set) and, on wake, drains ibv_get_async_event via responder_drain_async_event, naming events with async_event_name and logging fatal/error async events (QP_FATAL/QP_REQ_ERR/etc.). Best-effort operator diagnostics; no correctness FR mandates it.
proposals.rationale: Per drift-report suggested_spec: best-effort operator diagnostics, no FR needed unless it becomes load-bearing. Already backfilled into spec.md Known Limitations on 2026-08-07 (the 'Device async-event instrumentation' bullet), which also records the eprintln!-vs-ILogger gap tying to the FR-014 align-task. Verified present in the current spec; no additional spec edit required this run.

proposals.after: unchanged (verified faithful to current code; the eprintln! gap it documents is carried as the FR-014 ALIGN item above)
proposals.resolution: BACKFILL-UNSPECCED already satisfied by the existing Known Limitations bullet; no FR promotion (not load-bearing).

proposals.requirement: Unspecced: command-bridge thread (rdma-responder-cmd-bridge) draining the SPSC command inbox onto the command eventfd
proposals.actual: RealCmSeam spawns a dedicated bridge thread 'rdma-responder-cmd-bridge' that blocks on the SPSC command receiver and, per dequeued command, pushes it onto an internal Mutex<VecDeque> and signals the command eventfd (TAG_CMD) so the accept loop's epoll wakes. The SPSC channel has no pollable fd, so this bridge is the mechanism that realizes FR-004's 'command inbox' epoll wait arm. Mock seam has no bridge (delivers injected commands directly).
proposals.rationale: Per drift-report suggested_spec: note the FR-004 SPSC->eventfd bridge mechanism in plan.md/data-model. Behavior is implied by FR-004 but the bridge thread was an undocumented internal detail. Not a new user-facing FR; backfilled as an implementation note under FR-004 and as an internal entity in data-model.md.
proposals.before: FR-004 stated the epoll wait over {cm fd, command inbox, stop} with no note on how the fd-less SPSC command inbox is made pollable; data-model CM-seam section did not mention the bridge thread.
proposals.after: spec.md FR-004 gains a 'Command-inbox bridge note (backfilled 2026-08-20)' describing the SPSC->eventfd bridge thread; data-model.md gains a 'Command-inbox bridge thread' internal-entity subsection (role, lifecycle, mock-vs-real).
proposals.resolution: BACKFILL-UNSPECCED applied to spec.md (FR-004 note) and data-model.md (internal entity). No FR promotion — documents the FR-004 mechanism.
